eli: Heads-up — our sampleapp is getting stuck on pagination after we turned on the new adaptive client-side throttler. Requests queue up, no errors, then a big burst of 429s. Anyone seen this pattern?

jordan: which SDK / version?

eli: js-sdk 0.9.2 (fresh from npm). Config: 
```
throttler: {windowSize: 250, debounceMs: 50, maxInflight: 8, adaptive: true}
pagination: {pageSize: 100, cursorMode: true}
```
Logs look like: 
```
[2026-03-23T16:01:10Z] enqueued request id=az12 size=140
[2026-03-23T16:01:11Z] inflight=8 queued=72
[2026-03-23T16:01:11Z] upstream 429 model=redwood-mini
[2026-03-23T16:01:12Z] token-refresh start id=az12
[2026-03-23T16:01:12Z] duplicate send id=az12 (race)
```

priya: hmm. two quick things to try: 1) disable adaptive=true and see if static window avoids the queue growth; 2) check whether token refresh is re-sending requests without acquiring a refresh lock. The log line "token-refresh start" followed by "duplicate send" smells like an auth race (we had that in onboarding samples).

eli: tried disabling adaptive -> queue stays bounded but latency spikes. Token refresh looks suspicious: multiple parallel refresh attempts for the same session. Our refresh code uses naive await fetchToken() in each request path.

priya: yup — fix is to centralize refresh with a promise-lock. Example pattern: 
```
let refreshPromise = null;
async function getToken() {
  if (!isExpired()) return cached;
  if (!refreshPromise) refreshPromise = doRefresh();
  try { return await refreshPromise; } finally { refreshPromise = null; }
}
```
That prevents multiple inflight retries which blow up client-side queue when backpressure is tight.

eli: added lock, pushed test — better but still seeing bursts when cursor pagination auto-fetches next page on success. It happily pushes next requests until inflight limit then queues, then token refresh churn causes duplicate sends again (some edge where page success callback triggers before inflight counter decremented).

sven: runtime person here — two notes: 1) SDK should decrement inflight counter before invoking user callback that may trigger subsequent fetches (we've seen callback-induced bursts). 2) adaptive algorithm currently increases window aggressively on success; with cursor mode you get cascading growth. Try making success->growth slower (e.g., increase growth factor or add jitter).

eli: good call. Where's the minimal config change to slow growth?

sven: reduce window growth to +1 per success and add exponential backoff for consecutive refreshes. Example tweak: `growthFactor: 1, maxGrowthPerSec: 2, debounceJitterMs: 20` — also set `maxInflight` to a conservative 6 in sampleapps.

jordan: filing a quick SDK issue and PR to: 1) ensure inflight-- happens before user callbacks, 2) add optional token-refresh lock helper, 3) expose growthFactor & jitter knobs. Will reference this thread. :thumbsup:

eli: thanks — applying inflight decrement fix locally now. Also added `debounceJitterMs: 30` and `maxInflight: 6` to sampleapp — immediate improvement, queue growth curbed.

priya: we should add a short onboarding note in samples/docs: "If you use cursor pagination with adaptive throttling, prefer lower initial window and enable token refresh lock; otherwise callbacks can cascade requests." I can draft.

sdk-bot: Created issue #4521 and PR #4529 (wip) for inflight-decrement and refresh-lock. https://git.internal/redwood/sdk/pulls/4529 :robot_face:

eli: awesome. After tweaks, no more silent stalls. Leaving this thread for any follow-ups. Thanks y'all. :heart:
